name: RC15-H2: Data-dependent source distribution
theory: Lim et al. (2410.03229) prove data-dependent paths have lower variance velocity fields. Use persistence forecast (last history frame repeated 30x) as ODE source instead of N(0,I). Each training pair has different persistence-to-future displacement, so diversity comes from the velocity field.
target: Faster convergence, equal or better sample quality vs 152e.
falsification: After 100 epochs: eff_rank < 3.0 OR KS < 15/25 → data-dependent source doesn't work at our scale.
diagnostic_plan: 1. Training convergence: loss curve vs 152e — at which epoch does quality match?
2. Full metric table vs 152e: eff_rank, PC1-5, KS, kurtosis, Frobenius
3. Velocity field variance at t=0.5: compare with 152e (Lim predicts LOWER)
4. Spread analysis: is ensemble spread narrower than 152e?
5. If UNEXPECTED: generate at intermediate ODE steps (t=0.25, 0.5, 0.75)
learn_from_failure: Diversity depends on noise-to-data distance. Persistence source too deterministic. Would contradict Lim et al. at our scale.

name: RC15-H1-S1: Conditional one-shot FM with concatenation
theory: FMAP (2504.03463) validates concatenation conditioning for spatial attention + FM. Encoder output (128-dim) projected and concatenated as additional features per token. Preserves attention's ability to learn cross-cell correlations (unlike FiLM which modulates globally).
falsification: PC1 < 0.95 OR kurtosis < 0.5 after 200 epochs → conditioning fundamentally problematic for one-shot FM.
diagnostic_plan: 1. Full metric table vs 152e: eff_rank, PC1-5, KS, kurtosis, Frobenius
2. Conditionality: turb/calm width ratio on 50 turb + 50 calm windows
3. Condition ablation: random vs real condition — delta in every metric
4. Per-horizon breakdown: eff_rank and CI at h=1, h=15, h=30
5. Encoder output variance across test set
6. PC alignment per-horizon

learn_from_failure.PC1_degrades: Condition constrains dominant factor too much. Try condition dropout.
learn_from_failure.kurtosis_degrades: Condition makes velocity too deterministic. Try condition augmentation noise.
learn_from_failure.conditionality_fails: 128-dim bottleneck insufficient for 750-dim. Need cross-attention over history.

name: RC15-H1-S2: Residual prediction from persistence
theory: FMAP predicts delta = future - baseline. Reduces ODE transport distance, improves convergence, requires fewer steps. For us: delta = future - persistence (last history frame repeated).
target: Faster convergence. KS >= 15/25. Kurtosis may improve.
falsification: KS daily < 15/25 → residual transformation changes distribution too much.
diagnostic_plan: 1. Convergence comparison: loss at ep50, ep100, ep200 vs Stage 1
2. Full metric table vs Stage 1
3. Residual distribution histogram at h=1 and h=30 vs absolute
4. Level bias check: per-cell mean(gen) vs mean(GT) after adding persistence back
5. KS on levels AND KS on changes — report both
learn_from_failure: Residual distribution harder to model (more peaked or heavier-tailed). Absolute is better for this data.

name: RC15-H1-S3: Per-horizon learned scale
theory: FMAP rescales FM output by lead-time-dependent error scale. Add nn.Parameter(30) as per-horizon multiplier on velocity output. Trains jointly with velocity network via CFM loss backprop.
target: Spread ratio h30/h1 > 1.1. Growing uncertainty with horizon.
falsification: All scale values in [0.95, 1.05] → no effect. OR spread ratio < 1.05.
diagnostic_plan: 1. Learned scale values: plot scale_h vs horizon h
2. Spread curve: ensemble std vs horizon, compare GT and previous stages
3. Per-horizon eff_rank at h=1, h=15, h=30
4. Per-horizon kurtosis at h=1, h=15, h=30
5. Full metric table vs previous stages
learn_from_failure: CFM loss has no horizon-dependent gradient. Would need explicit spread loss (VS/IS), raising paradigm conflict question.
